# zyxel_acl_rule (Resource)

Manages one firewall ACL entry in the router's `firewall_acl` table. Interface selection is fixed to `ALL`, and schedule rules are not exposed yet. The protocol can be `all`, `tcp_udp`, `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, or `icmpv6`; the address family can be IPv4 or IPv6. MAC, custom service, TCP flag, and direction filters are supported. Optional packet rate limiting is supported for `accept` rules. Existing rows must be imported by exact name; imported rows outside this supported profile are rejected. Set order for strict numeric placement, or omit it to append and compute the observed position. Rule-field changes require replacement because no safe in-place update or reorder operation has been verified; removing configured order only relinquishes numeric position management. Append cannot maintain a separate trailing drop set; use zyxel_acl_policy for an ordered accept list plus explicit drop_rules. See the ACL ordering and recovery guide. The router applies order globally; this resource does not guarantee a complete firewall policy across independent resources or Terraform states.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Addresses and MACs are documentation placeholders. Choose unused ACL positions
# after reviewing your router's complete rule table before applying.
resource "zyxel_service" "https" {
  name              = "HTTPS"
  description       = "Secure web"
  protocol          = "tcp"
  source_ports      = "*"
  destination_ports = "443"
}

resource "zyxel_acl_rule" "https" {
  name              = "Allow-HTTPS-Example"
  action            = "accept"
  order             = 10
  source_cidr       = "198.51.100.0/24"
  destination_cidr  = "192.0.2.10/32"
  source_ports      = "*"
  destination_ports = "443"
  packets_per_unit  = 100
  rate_limit_unit   = "minute"
}

resource "zyxel_acl_rule" "ipv6_https" {
  name                   = "Allow-IPv6-HTTPS-Example"
  action                 = "accept"
  order                  = 11
  ip_version             = "ipv6"
  direction              = "lan_to_wan"
  source_cidr            = "2001:db8:1::/64"
  destination_cidr       = "2001:db8:2::10/128"
  destination_port_start = 443
  destination_port_end   = 443
}

resource "zyxel_acl_rule" "restricted_client" {
  name             = "Restricted-Client-Example"
  action           = "reject"
  order            = 12
  direction        = "lan_to_wan"
  mac_address      = "02:00:00:00:00:20"
  source_cidr      = "192.0.2.0/24"
  destination_cidr = "198.51.100.10/32"
  protocol         = "tcp_udp"
  tcp_flag         = "syn"
}

# A custom service replaces inline protocol and port filters.
resource "zyxel_acl_rule" "https_service" {
  name             = "Allow-HTTPS-Service-Example"
  action           = "accept"
  order            = 13
  source_cidr      = "198.51.100.0/24"
  destination_cidr = "192.0.2.10/32"
  service_id       = zyxel_service.https.id
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `action` (String) ACL action: `accept`, `drop`, or `reject`. The router stores these as `Accept`, `Drop`, or `Reject`.
- `destination_cidr` (String) Canonical destination CIDR in the selected `ip_version`. Changing it replaces the ACL rule.
- `name` (String) Exact, non-empty router rule name. This is the natural identity and import key; duplicate names are ambiguous.

### Optional

- `destination_port_end` (Number) Port from 1 through 65535; the range end must be at least the start. Set both bounds or omit both for any port. Ports are only used by the `tcp`, `udp`, and `tcp_udp` protocols. Changing it replaces the ACL rule.
- `destination_port_start` (Number) Port from 1 through 65535; the range end must be at least the start. Set both bounds or omit both for any port. Ports are only used by the `tcp`, `udp`, and `tcp_udp` protocols. Changing it replaces the ACL rule.
- `destination_ports` (String) Destination ports: `*` (any), `443` (single), or `443-445` (inclusive range). Conflicts with numeric destination port bounds and `service_id`. TCP/UDP protocols only. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `direction` (String) Traffic direction: `wan_to_lan`, `lan_to_wan`, `wan_to_router`, or `lan_to_router`. Defaults to `wan_to_lan`. Changing it replaces the ACL rule. Observed firmware limitation: `lan_to_router` rules do not block LAN-to-router access, even with `drop` or `reject`; devices on the LAN can still reach the router through its LAN interface.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the ACL rule is enabled. Defaults to `true`; changing it replaces the rule.
- `ip_version` (String) Address family for `source_cidr` and `destination_cidr`: `ipv4` or `ipv6`. Defaults to `ipv4`. With `ipv6` you must set both CIDRs explicitly to IPv6 networks because the default source remains `0.0.0.0/0`. Changing it replaces the ACL rule.
- `mac_address` (String) Optional source MAC address filter in canonical uppercase six-octet colon-separated form (for example, `02:00:00:00:00:20`). Omit for any MAC address. Changing it replaces the ACL rule.
- `order` (Number) Set a positive value for strict ordering: occupied positions are rejected and readback must match exactly. Omit (or set null) to append at max current order + 1 and record the observed firmware-assigned position, accepting compaction without replacement. Append verifies the rule is last and refuses accepts behind any enabled drop/reject or unknown action, even unrelated ones. No insertion/reorder or ongoing trailing-drop policy management is supported; see the ordering and recovery guide.
- `packets_per_unit` (Number) Optional packet rate limit: number of matching packets allowed per `rate_limit_unit`, from 1 through 512. Omit to disable rate limiting. Rate limiting requires `action = "accept"` and changing it replaces the ACL rule.
- `protocol` (String) Transport protocol: `all`, `tcp_udp`, `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, or `icmpv6`. Defaults to `tcp` for inline rules. Omit when using `service_id`; the neutral `all` value is then computed and the service selects the protocol. Changing it replaces the ACL rule.
- `rate_limit_unit` (String) Time period for `packets_per_unit`: `minute` or `second`. Defaults to `minute`; only used when `packets_per_unit` is set. Changing it replaces the ACL rule.
- `service` (String) Optional name of a custom protocol/service group on the router. Omit for none. The service must already exist; this resource does not create it. Changing it replaces the ACL rule.
- `service_id` (String) Native custom service ID, for example `zyxel_service.https.id`. Mutually exclusive with `service` and inline protocol/port/TCP flag settings. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `source_cidr` (String) Canonical source CIDR in the selected `ip_version`. Defaults to `0.0.0.0/0` (any IPv4 source). Use the canonical network address for the prefix; changing it replaces the rule.
- `source_port_end` (Number) Optional source port range end. Set this together with `source_port_start`; changing it replaces the ACL rule.
- `source_port_start` (Number) Optional source port range start for the `tcp`, `udp`, and `tcp_udp` protocols. Leave both source port bounds null for any source port; null maps to router values `-1/-1`.
- `source_ports` (String) Source ports: `*` (any), `443` (single), or `443-445` (inclusive range). Conflicts with numeric source port bounds and `service_id`. TCP/UDP protocols only. Changing it replaces the rule.
- `tcp_flag` (String) Optional TCP flag to match: `syn`, `ack`, `urg`, `psh`, `rst`, or `fin`. Omit for any flag. Only valid with the `tcp` and `tcp_udp` protocols. Changing it replaces the ACL rule.

### Read-Only

- `router_index` (Number) Current router list index, exposed for diagnostics only. Indexes shift after deletes and are never used as resource identity.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import zyxel_acl_rule.https 'Allow-HTTPS-Example'
```
